mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate above 8.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 8.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based contraction in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenue expectations decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) signals supply chain disruptions and reduced manufacturing output, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher input costs and lower corporate margins.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: A consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annual inflation rate signals inflationary pressures that prompt monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as real interest rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in less than 45% of periods when CPIAUCSL indicates annual inflation above 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 100,000 indicates weak labor market growth that reduces corporate hiring expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS < 100000.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a strong but potentially overheating economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as growth expectations rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both CPIAUCSL and HOUST increase.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) and rising unemployment (UNRATE > 8.0) signal a dual recessionary pressure on supply and labor markets, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0 AND UNRATE > 8.0.
